core_meaning.short_meaning: Joyful heart, clear expositor; famed Islamic judge Shurayh al-Qadi.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Shurayh (شُرَيْح) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'one who brings joyful clarity', 'relieved of distress', or 'the clear, open explanation'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Shurayh ibn al-Harith al-Kindi (al-Qadi Shurayh), the legendary judge of Kufa famed for unwavering justice.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive of sharḥ (expansion, explanation, relief), signifying a light, joyous, and serene spirit.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root sh-r-ḥ denotes opening, expanding, and clarifying, as in the Quranic concept of 'sharh al-sadr' (expansion of the heart with faith). As a proper name, Shurayh al-Qadi was appointed judge of Kufa by Umar ibn al-Khattab and served for over sixty years under Ali ibn Abi Talib and subsequent leaders, legendary for ruling impartially even against caliphs.
